messages.content: How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?

function.name: calculate_vector_angle
function.description: Calculate the angle of a vector based on its X and Y components. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

X_component.description: The X component of the vector. This is a float type value.

Y_component.description: The Y component of the vector. This is a float type value.

use_degrees.description: If true, the result will be in degrees. If false, the result will be in radians. Default is false.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?" They want to find the angle of the force for a given momentum. We need to interpret what they mean. They might be asking about the relationship between force and momentum. Force is the time derivative of momentum: F = dp/dt. The direction of force is the direction of change of momentum. So if we have momentum vector p(t) at two times, we can compute the change Δp over Δt, then the average force direction is Δp/|Δp|. But maybe they want to find the angle of the force vector relative to some axis given the momentum vector. But the question is ambiguous. They might want to find the angle of the force vector given the momentum vector. But we need to ask clarifying questions. The user didn't specify any numeric values or context. So we should ask clarifying questions: Are you given the momentum vector components? Are you given the force vector components? Are you given the time interval? Or do you want to find the angle of the force vector relative to the momentum vector? Or relative to some axis? Also, do you want to use degrees or radians? We can ask them to provide the X and Y components of the vector. But the user didn't mention any vector. They just said "force for a given momentum". So we need to clarify what exactly they want. We can ask: "Do you have the components of the momentum vector? And do you want the angle of the force vector relative to the x-axis?" Also, we can ask if they want the angle in degrees or radians. So we should ask clarifying questions.
